newsitem.title: USA: Depression becomes tropical storm Claudette off U.S..
newsitem.headline: Depression becomes tropical storm Claudette off U.S..

text.p: The third tropical storm of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season formed east of the U.S. coast Sunday, a day after the season's first hurricane, Bill, faded in the northern Atlantic.
As of 5 p.m. (2100 GMT), the weather system spinning west of Bermuda had strengthened enough to become Tropical Storm Claudette, the National Hurricane Centre said.

Its centre was near latitude 32.2 north and longitude 72.9 west, or about 280 miles (451 km) south-southeast of Cape Hatteras, N.C., and 480 miles (772 km) west of Bermuda, the National Hurricane Centre said.
The system was nearly stationary, but forecasters said they expected it to begin drifting northward Sunday night.

Maximum sustained winds were near 45 mph (72 kph), with higher gusts, and some strengthening was expected during the next 24 hours. Tropical storm force winds extended up to 50 miles (80 km) to the east of Claudette's centre.
Claudette would become a hurricane if maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
